title: Whose Fix Made It?

narrative.intro: Two devs, same sprint, same bug tracker. Priya branched off to fix a null-check crash on checkout. Sam branched off separately to fix a race condition in the save queue. Standup this morning: "both fixes are merged into main, ready for release." You pull up the graph to confirm before you sign off on it.
narrative.correctDebrief: Correct - only Priya's fix actually landed. Look at the commit on main: its message claims both fixes got combined, but it only has one parent - Priya's tip. Sam's commit still exists, signed and all, but it's sitting on its own unreferenced branch, unreachable from main. Nobody lied on purpose, probably - someone force-pushed, squashed, or fast-forwarded wrong. Either way: without Version Control actually tracking full merge ancestry (not just trusting a commit message), "both fixes are merged" was just wrong, and nobody would've caught it without walking the graph.
narrative.incorrectDebrief: Check the merge commit's parents, not its message. A commit message can claim anything - what actually determines whether a change is "in" is whether its commit is an ancestor of HEAD. Trace main's parentIds back and see which branch tip it actually connects to.
